title: Fin Trading — SSE Lifecycle Reference
description: Static reference explaining the thread/node/task lifecycle and the ACK mechanism used by SSE notifications.

options.content:
## SSE Notification Scope Hierarchy

Every user query runs in a **Thread**. A thread executes a sequence of **Nodes** (LangGraph graph nodes). Each node may dispatch one or more **Tasks** (Celery workers).

```
Thread  ─── Node ─── Task
              └────── Task
        ─── Node ─── Task
```

### Why ACK?

SSE is fire-and-forget at the transport layer. Without an application-level ACK the backend cannot know whether the frontend actually received and rendered the event.
The ACK loop ensures **at-least-once delivery**: the backend republishes the event every `retry_interval` seconds (default **5 s**) for up to `max_retries` attempts (default **6**, i.e. up to 30 s total) until the frontend confirms receipt.

This is especially important for terminal lifecycle events (`done`, `node_status: completed`, `task_status: completed/failed`) because missing one leaves the UI in a stale state.

## Thread Lifecycle

A **thread** represents the full execution of one user query.

### Typical event sequence

| Step | Event | ACK required? | Notes |
|------|-------|---------------|-------|
| 1 | `query_status: submitted` | ✅ Yes | Emitted right after the query is accepted; confirms the backend received the request |
| 2 | *(nodes execute — see Node tab)* | — | — |
| 3 | `done: completed` | ✅ Yes | Terminal success; signals the frontend to close the SSE channel |
| 3 | `done: failed` | ✅ Yes | Terminal failure |
| 3 | `done: cancelled` | ✅ Yes | User-initiated cancellation |

### No-viewer fast path

If the app has no active clients (`has_app_viewers = False`), the graph keeps running silently — no events are published at all.

If clients are connected but none are viewing this specific thread (`has_thread_viewers = False`), the event is published **once** (stored in Centrifugo history for recovery when the user navigates back) and the ACK loop is skipped. This is recorded as **`result = skipped / reason = no_thread_viewers`** in the audit.

### Scope: `thread`

- Published to the **thread-level Centrifugo channel** (`thread:{thread_id}`).
- Envelope fields: `thread_id`, `event`, `status`, `metadata`, `content`, `ack_key`.
- ACK key default: `thread:{event}:{status}:{nonce}`

## Node Lifecycle

A **node** is a single LangGraph graph node execution within a thread version.

### Typical event sequence

| Step | Event | ACK required? | Notes |
|------|-------|---------------|-------|
| 1 | `node_status: running` | 🔕 No (fire-and-forget) | Published at node entry; backend does not block waiting for ACK. Used only for live progress indication. |
| 2 | *(tasks execute — see Task tab)* | — | — |
| 3 | `node_status: completed` | ✅ Yes | Published by `_complete_node_internal` in lifecycle ops |
| 3 | `node_status: failed` | ✅ Yes | Published on unhandled node exception |
| 3 | `node_status: cancelled` | ✅ Yes | Published when the thread cancellation flag is set |

### `require_ack=False` path

Node-scope events with `require_ack=False` are fire-and-forget. The metric counter `sse_notification_publish_total{scope="node"}` is still incremented so publish volume is tracked even for fire-and-forget events.

### Scope: `node`

- Published to the **node-level Centrifugo channel** (`node:{thread_id}`).
- Envelope fields: `thread_id`, `node_id`, `node_name`, `event`, `status`, `metadata`, `content`, `ack_key`.
- ACK key default: `node:{node_id}:{event}:{nonce}`

## Task Lifecycle

A **task** is a single Celery worker execution dispatched by a node (via `delegate_task`). Tasks run concurrently and report their own SSE events.

### Typical event sequence

| Step | Event | `status` | ACK required? | Notes |
|------|-------|----------|---------------|-------|
| 1 | `task_status` | `running` | 🔕 No | Emitted when the worker picks up the task |
| 2 | `task_status` | `streaming` | 🔕 No | Emitted for each LLM stream chunk (high frequency) |
| 3 | `task_status` | `completed` | ✅ Yes | Terminal success — emitted by `delegate_completion` before node-level SSE fires |
| 3 | `task_status` | `failed` | ✅ Yes | Terminal failure |
| 3 | `task_status` | `cancelled` | ✅ Yes | Worker cancelled by thread cancellation |

### Ordering guarantee

Task terminal events (`completed`/`failed`) are published **and ACKed** inside `delegate_completion` **before** the owning node fires its own `node_status: completed` SSE. This enforces strict frontend rendering order: task → node → thread.

### Exhausted ACK → auto-fail

Unlike node-scope where exhaustion publishes `notification_failed`, task-scope exhaustion publishes `task_status: failed` with `reason: ack_timeout` so the frontend always receives a deterministic terminal status for the task.

### Scope: `task`

- Published to the **thread-level Centrifugo channel** (same channel as thread events — `thread:{thread_id}`).
- Envelope fields: `thread_id`, `task_id`, `node_id`, `node_name`, `task_name`, `event`, `status`, `view_type`, `stats_views`, `content`, `ack_key`.
- ACK key default: `task:{task_id}:{event}:{nonce}`

## ACK Flow (per event)

```
 Backend                               Redis                    Frontend
 ───────                               ─────                    ────────
 1. Generate nonce → ack_key
 2. Publish event to Centrifugo ──────────────────────────────► receives event
    (with ack_key in payload)
 3. BLPOP sse_ack:{thread_id}:{ack_key}
    (timeout = retry_interval, default 5 s)
                                                                 4. Process event
                                                                    (render UI)
                                                                 5. POST /api/v1/sse/ack
                                                                    { ack_key, thread_id }
                               ◄── LPUSH sse_ack:{thread_id}:{ack_key} ──
 6. BLPOP returns "ack"
    → return True
```

### NACK

The frontend sends `POST /api/v1/sse/ack` with `{ ack_key, nack: true }` when it cannot process the event (e.g. the thread panel was closed). The backend BLPOP reads `"nack"` and records the failure in Prometheus counters.

### Exhaustion

If BLPOP times out on every attempt (retry loop exhausted):
- `sse_notification_nack_total{reason="exhausted"}` is incremented.
- A `notification_failed` event (node scope) or `task_status: failed` (task scope) is published so the frontend can recover.

### Redis ACK key

```
sse_ack:{thread_id}:{ack_key}    ← backend BLPOPs, frontend LPUSHes
```

## ACK Outcomes (tracked in Prometheus)

| Outcome | Prometheus counter | Meaning |
|---------|-------------------|--------|
| ACK | `sse_notification_ack_total` | Frontend confirmed receipt within retry budget |
| NACK (explicit) | `sse_notification_nack_total{reason="explicit_nack"}` | Frontend explicitly rejected |
| NACK (exhausted) | `sse_notification_nack_total{reason="exhausted"}` | All `max_retries` (6) attempts timed out |

## Prometheus Metrics

| Metric | Labels | Description |
|--------|--------|-------------|
| `sse_notification_publish_total` | `scope`, `event` | Every publish attempt (1 per event per attempt) |
| `sse_notification_attempt_total` | `scope`, `event` | Publish attempts inside the retry loop (excludes fire-and-forget) |
| `sse_notification_ack_total` | `scope`, `event` | ACKs received |
| `sse_notification_nack_total` | `scope`, `event`, `reason` | NACKs (explicit or exhausted) |
| `sse_notification_ack_latency_seconds` | `scope`, `event` | Histogram of total time from first publish to ACK |

## Centrifugo Channel Mapping

| Scope | Centrifugo Channel | Publisher function |
|-------|-------------------|-------------------|
| Thread | `thread:{thread_id}` | `publish_thread_event` |
| Node | `node:{thread_id}` | `publish_node_event` |
| Task | `thread:{thread_id}` | `publish_task_event` (shared with thread channel) |

The **SSE tier** (centrifugo-sse-0/1, ports 8103/8104) handles all lifecycle events.
The **LLM tier** (centrifugo-llm-0/1, ports 8101/8102) handles token streaming.

The frontend subscribes to both `thread:{thread_id}` and `node:{thread_id}` when opening a thread panel.

### ACK Redis key

```
sse_ack:{thread_id}:{ack_key}    <- backend BLPOPs, frontend LPUSHes
```

## Reading the SSE Audit Dashboard

Open **Fin Trading — SSE Notification Audit** (`fin-sse-audit`) for live metrics.

### Key panels

| Panel | What to look for |
|-------|------------------|
| **ACK % by scope (gauge)** | Should be ≥ 95 % in normal operation. Drops indicate frontend connectivity issues or high load. |
| **ACK % over time** | Sudden drops correlate with deployments or network instability. |
| **NACK rate by reason** | `exhausted` NACKs mean the frontend is too slow or disconnected. `explicit_nack` means the UI intentionally rejected. |
| **ACK latency p95** | Should be < 1 s for active viewers. Spikes mean the frontend event loop is blocked. |
| **Retry pressure** | `attempt_total / publish_total > 1` means events are being retried — watch for sustained pressure. |

### Filtering by thread/node/task

Use the `$thread_id`, `$node_id`, and `$task_id` template variables to drill down to specific execution contexts. The Loki log panels in the lower half of the audit dashboard show raw SSE lifecycle logs filtered by those IDs.

### Link to this dashboard

Bookmark: `http://localhost:3210/d/fin-sse-lifecycle-ref`
Audit dashboard: `http://localhost:3210/d/fin-sse-audit`
